title: Kafka Failures and Retries
summary: Handle publish failures, consumer retries, durable pending events, and duplicate delivery.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Kafka Fallback: What if Kafka doesn't work ?

richText: Distinguish publication from processing
Publishing to Kafka and processing a received record are separate operations. Each can fail independently.
KafkaTemplate.send can throw immediately or complete its future with an error later.
A try/catch around send alone cannot catch a later asynchronous failure. Inspect the future or use a completion callback.
A timeout means the caller stopped waiting. It does not prove that the broker rejected the record.
Sending an email directly after a publish timeout can duplicate an email later sent by the consumer.
Store work before retrying publication
An outbox is a database record for an event that still needs to be published.
When possible, save the business change and outbox record in the same database transaction.
A background worker publishes pending outbox records. It marks them published after broker acknowledgment.
A crash between publication and marking the record can cause another publication. Consumers still need duplicate handling.
Report a queued state only after durable storage succeeds. If storage fails, report failure. Logging an event does not preserve it.
Retry a failed consumer
Let exceptions escape the listener so the container can detect failure.
DefaultErrorHandler can retry temporary processing failures. Configure a limit.
Backoff is the wait between attempts. One initial attempt plus two retries means three attempts in total.
Do not retry invalid event formats or permanent business errors without correcting them.
A dead-letter topic stores records that could not be processed after the allowed attempts.
DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer publishes those failed records. Ensure publication succeeds before treating recovery as complete.
Monitor failed records, retries, and consumer lag. Consumer lag is how far consumption is behind available records.
Understand duplicate handling limits
Producer idempotence prevents certain duplicate Kafka writes caused by producer retries. It does not make an external action happen once.
Kafka transactions can provide exactly-once results for supported Kafka read-process-write flows. Ordinary SMTP is outside that transaction.
A stable event ID lets a consumer identify repeated work.
Sending an email before recording completion risks a duplicate after a crash. Recording completion first risks losing the email.
Use idempotent mail submission when the provider supports it. Otherwise choose and document the remaining retry and duplicate behavior.
